findings.reason: The protected source is the exact integer quadratic formula in its clearest Python form. math.isqrt avoids floating-point boundary risk, the arithmetic mirrors the derived positive root directly, and no temporary state or control flow is needed. No inert candidate would materially improve this one-line solution.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 441 and its Python integer-to-integer surface. The app solve signature and native arrangeCoins method use the same positive coin count and return the same maximum number of complete rows. The modular Reference preserves both current source examples and explanations, the incomplete-last-row rule, and the single signed-32-bit constraint.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064823188. The app and native implementations import the same integer square root and return the identical expression (isqrt(1 + 8 * n) - 1) // 2; only the required Solution wrapper differs.

The 256-, 1024-, and 4096-row tiers span 16x and scale the triangular coin total while the exact bounded-integer formula remains fixed work. The protected source passed all 10 opaque correctness executions and all three performance tiers at 1.03x the reference runtime. A correct chunked O(sqrt(n)) row-subtraction control passed every output but failed only the runtime verdict at 3.22x.

The Approach exactly derives the triangular inequality, solves its positive quadratic root, explains integer-square-root flooring and maximum feasibility, states fixed-domain O(1) time and O(1) space, and covers triangular boundaries, leftovers, and the one-coin minimum.

The hash-bound Reference was checked against the live public statement. It preserves the staircase rule, possibly incomplete last row, both exact examples and explanations, and the sole constraint. Two independently authored accessible tables reproduce the row-by-row coin placement and complete/incomplete status of both provider images.
